title: Activation-to-Renewal Scoring Workbench
body:
Purpose

This is a working doc for an operational health scoring workbench that spans from initial activation through renewal. Goal: produce a lightweight, actionable score and triage flow we can run weekly and surface in CSM dashboards and QBR packs. This is intentionally pragmatic and metric-driven; thresholds and weights below are proposals for experimentation.

Scope and intended use
- Covers customers in first 0-18 months after go-live (activation -> expansion -> renewal cycle).
- Output: single numeric Health Index (0-100), top 3 risk flags, recommended playbook actions, and QBR talking points.
- To be computed weekly and stored as a row per customer for trend analysis.

High-level model (proposed)
Health Index composition (weights add to 100):
- Activation completeness: 0-25 (setup tasks, integrations, success milestones) - weight 25
- Product engagement: 0-35 (DAU/WAU, feature depth, API call distribution) - weight 35
- Support friction: 0-20 (open P1/P2 tickets, time to resolution, escalation count) - weight 20
- Business impact & advocacy: 0-20 (executive engagement, ROI signals, NPS/CSAT) - weight 20

Scoring rules (quick rubric)
- Activation completeness (0-25): each milestone 5 points (5 milestones). If integration required but not completed, cap at 10. If customer has service-level onboarding support flagged as incomplete, subtract 5.
- Product engagement (0-35): measure 3 dimensions: frequency, breadth, depth. Normalize each to 0-100, average, scale to 35. Example thresholds: frequency (DAU/WAU) drop >30% vs prior 4 weeks => subtract 10 points. Breadth: number of distinct endpoints used. Depth: avg tokens per session or long-run inference usage.
- Support friction (0-20): open critical tickets older than 72 hours => automatic -10 to score; repeated regressions on same issue => -5; support satisfaction survey below 6 => -5.
- Business impact & advocacy (0-20): regular exec touchpoints in last 90 days => +10; case studies or ROI model completed => +10; procurement signals for renewal (e.g., renewals team engaged) => +5.

Health buckets (operational thresholds)
- Healthy: Index >= 80. Watch: Index 60-79. At risk: Index 40-59. Churn risk: Index < 40.
- Note: single severe flag (P1 unresolved 7+ days OR exec disengaged for >120 days) should escalate regardless of numeric bucket.

Risk flag taxonomy (examples we will compute and expose)
- Activation lag: onboarding milestone overdue > 14 days past plan
- Usage decline: rolling 28-day DAU down > 30% vs prior 28-day period
- Narrowing usage: > 80% of requests hitting a single endpoint (indicates single-use case fragility)
- Support entropy: >=2 P1/P2 regressions in last 30 days OR any P1 open >72h
- Exec disengaged: no executive or champion touchpoint > 90 days
- Contract exposure: procurement or legal delays flagged in notes or renewal date < 90 days without plan
- Low ROI evidence: customer not using billing-sensitive features or no business metrics mapped

Playbook actions by primary flag (CSM quick steps)
- Activation lag:
  - Action: schedule 2-week onboarding sprint, assign SE shadow, propose checklist-based POA.
  - Owner: Onboarding SE + CSM. Slack channel: #onboard-escalations.
- Usage decline:
  - Action: run product funnel analysis, identify missing component, propose targeted re-engagement campaign (sample scripts below).
  - Owner: CSM + Solutions Eng. Consider feature walkthrough + technical office hours.
- Narrowing usage:
  - Action: workshop potential expansion opportunities, map additional business workflows, present 2-3 quick wins for month.
  - Owner: CSM, AM if ARR >100k.
- Support entropy:
  - Action: mandatory P1 postmortem w/ SRE and TPM; prioritize fix track; weekly status until resolved.
  - Owner: CSM escalation + SRE on call.
- Exec disengaged:
  - Action: prep ROI snapshot and calendar invite for exec briefing, include product roadmap items aligned to their KPIs.
  - Owner: CSM + Customer Success Lead.

QBR content checklist (to include when Health Index is below 80 or customer is a strategic account)
- One-page health summary: current index, month trend, top 3 flags and actions.
- Usage trends: DAU/WAU, top endpoints, cohort retention by feature.
- Support summary: open tickets, outstanding blockers, average TTR.
- Business outcomes: metrics customer tracks that LLM features impact (e.g., support deflection %, conversion lift).
- Roadmap alignment: 3 items prioritized for next 90 days.
- Renewal plan: current contract dates, decision maker list, negotiation window.

Sample worksheet (CSV rows we will store per customer per week)
- columns: customer_id, week_start, health_index, activation_score, engagement_score, support_score, impact_score, top_flag_1, top_flag_2, top_flag_3, notes
- sample row: CUST-332,2026-02-09,72,20,28,12,12,usage_decline,exec_disengaged,activation_lag,Reached out to PE team for SDR workshop

Signals instrumentation notes
- Most signals can be computed from existing telemetry: API call logs, auth events (for DAU), support ticket system, NPS/CSAT, calendar metadata (touchpoints).
- Missing pieces: exec touchpoint tracking (CSM manual input or calendar integration), ROI evidence capture (CSM form to attach ROI docs).

Dashboard and alerting suggestions
- Weekly job computes Health Index and writes to CS data table.
- Triggers: index drop > 15 points week-over-week => Slack alert to CSM + lead; any P1 open >72h => page on-call; exec disengaged flag => task in CSM queue.

QBR prompts for CSM to prepare (boilerplate text)
- What were the 3 biggest wins since last QBR?
- What are the remaining blockers to realizing predicted ROI?
- Which product areas should we prioritize for Q2 to increase usage depth?

Notes, assumptions, and open questions
- Assumption: telemetry feeds are viable and batched daily. If not, index will be computed weekly with gaps.
- Open: how to reliably capture exec touchpoints without extra CSM burden? Ideas: calendar-scanner with opt-in or quick CSM one-click logging.
- Open: do we want to weight enterprise customers differently (e.g., attach ARR multiplier)? Pros: prioritize high-value customers. Cons: hides organic health signals.

Next steps (minimal MVP)
1. Implement weekly ETL that produces the CSV row per customer for last 90 days (data engineering).
2. Pilot model on 30 strategic customers for 8 weeks; collect qualitative feedback from CSMs.
3. Iterate weights and thresholds; codify playbook actions into the CS playbook repo.
4. Add basic dashboard tile to CSM console and weekly alerting.

Notes to self
- Keep the model interpretable; CSMs must be able to explain why a customer moved buckets.
- Avoid too many micro-flags; aim for 6-8 core flags.
- We should include a short training session for CSMs before pilot launch.

References and links
- Confluence: activation-to-renewal health model page (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-CS-789 for pilot tracking
- Repo: github.com/redwood/cs-playbooks (PR 42 contains initial playbook scripts)

End of workbench draft
